机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: OccamView enhances active 3D Gaussian reconstruction by integrating object-conditioned view selection with geometry-driven strategies, improving completion rates under limited sensing budgets.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Active 3D Gaussian reconstruction fundamentally relies on selecting informative next-best views under limited sensing budgets. Existing active 3DGS methods primarily plan viewpoints according to geometric information gain, treating object-induced hidden regions in the same manner as general unexplored space. Under tight frame budgets, such geometry-driven strategies may prioritize global scene coverage while leaving partially observed objects incompletely reconstructed. To address this limitation, we propose OccamView, an object-conditioned view-selection framework for frame-budgeted active 3D Gaussian reconstruction. Rather than predicting unseen object geometry or performing shape completion, OccamView maintains an online object memory from open-vocabulary detections grounded in measured RGB-D observations and represents unresolved local occupancy around detected objects as conservative hidden-region proxies. Candidate viewpoints are then evaluated using an occlusion-aware proxy-coverage score. Furthermore, we introduce a Geo-Floor mechanism that restricts object-conditioned re-ranking to geometrically competitive candidates, allowing object-conditioned cues to guide complementary observations while preserving the geometry-driven exploration behavior of the underlying planner. Experiments on Replica and Matterport3D under a unified frame-budgeted protocol show that OccamView consistently reduces Completion and improves Completion Ratio across five frame budgets, with particularly pronounced gains under limited frame budgets. These results demonstrate that lightweight object-conditioned cues effectively complement geometry-driven active view planning.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Towards Effective and Transferable Physical Camouflage against Multi-View BEV-based 3D Perception in Autonomous Driving
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Linye Lyu, Jiawei Zhou, Daojing He, Yu Li
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: The paper presents BEVCA, a novel framework for generating effective and transferable adversarial camouflage against multi-view BEV-based 3D perception in autonomous driving.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Modern autonomous driving systems widely adopt multi-view Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) based 3D perception models due to their superior performance. Despite their success, the robustness of these models against adversarial camouflage attacks remains largely unexplored. Existing camouflage attacks primarily target single-view 2D detectors, limiting their effectiveness in multi-view 3D perception settings. To address this gap, we propose BEVCA, a novel adversarial camouflage generation framework tailored for multi-view BEV-based 3D perception. Our framework integrates a BEV-feature-based adversarial loss with a multi-view neural rendering module, enabling effective and transferable camouflage attacks across different models and tasks. Extensive experiments in both digital and physical settings demonstrate that BEVCA outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and exhibits strong robustness under real-world conditions. Our code is available at https://github.com/WAVE-AT-IDEA/BEVCA.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: 3D Generation for Embodied AI and Robotic Simulation: A Survey
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Tianwei Ye, Yifan Mao, Minwen Liao, Jian Liu, Chunchao Guo
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: This survey explores the evolving role of 3D generation in embodied AI, emphasizing interaction readiness over visual realism and identifying key challenges for effective simulation and real-world application.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Embodied AI and robotic systems increasingly depend on scalable, diverse, and physically grounded 3D content for simulation-based training and real-world deployment. While 3D generative modeling has advanced rapidly, embodied applications impose requirements far beyond visual realism: generated objects must carry kinematic structure and material properties, scenes must support interaction and task execution, and the resulting content must bridge the gap between simulation and reality. This survey reviews 3D generation for embodied AI and organizes the literature around three roles that 3D generation plays in embodied systems. In Data Generator, 3D generation produces simulation-ready objects and assets, including articulated, physically grounded, and deformable content for downstream interaction; in Simulation Environments, it constructs interactive and task-oriented worlds, spanning structure-aware, controllable, and agentic scene generation; and in Sim2Real Bridge, it supports digital twin reconstruction, data augmentation, and synthetic demonstrations for downstream robot learning and real-world transfer. We also show that the field is shifting from visual realism toward interaction readiness, and we identify the main bottlenecks, including limited physical annotations, the gap between geometric quality and physical validity, fragmented evaluation, and the persistent sim-to-real divide, that must be addressed for 3D generation to become a dependable foundation for embodied intelligence. Our project page is at https://3dgen4robot.github.io.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: Seeing Through the Chain: Understanding and Mitigating Hallucinations in Multimodal Large Reasoning Models
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Hao Fang, Jinyu Li, Jiawei Kong, Tianqu Zhuang, Kuofeng Gao
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: This paper presents C3PO, a framework that mitigates hallucinations in multimodal reasoning models by enhancing reasoning quality and filtering redundant tokens for improved signal efficiency.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: While multimodal reasoning models (MLRMs) have exhibited impressive capabilities, they remain prone to hallucinations, and effective solutions are still underexplored. In this paper, we experimentally analyze the hallucination cause and propose C3PO, a training-based mitigation framework comprising \textbf{C}hain-of-Thought \textbf{C}ompression and \textbf{C}ontrastive \textbf{P}reference \textbf{O}ptimization. Firstly, we identify that introducing reasoning mechanisms exacerbates models' reliance on language priors while overlooking visual inputs, which can produce CoTs with reduced visual cues but redundant text tokens. To this end, we propose to selectively filter redundant thinking tokens for a more compact and signal-efficient CoT representation that preserves task-relevant information while suppressing noise. In addition, we observe that the quality of the reasoning trace largely determines whether hallucination emerges in subsequent responses. To leverage this insight, we introduce a reasoning-enhanced preference tuning scheme that constructs training pairs using high-quality AI feedback. We further design a multimodal hallucination-inducing mechanism that elicits models' inherent hallucination patterns via carefully crafted inducers, yielding informative negative signals for contrastive correction. We provide theoretical justification for the effectiveness and demonstrate consistent hallucination reduction across diverse MLRMs and benchmarks.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Sixiang Chen, Jiaming Liu, Jixian Wu, Yichen Guo, Tinghao Wang
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The paper introduces WorldEcho and WorldSync to evaluate and improve action-conditioned world models, enhancing their reliability for robotic policy learning by aligning generated futures with actual actions.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Action-conditioned world models increasingly serve as learned simulators for robotic policy improvement, yet their reliability rests on an unverified assumption: generated futures faithfully reflect the consequences of arbitrary valid actions. Systematic evaluation against action-specific ground truth remains limited beyond expert demonstrations. To address this gap, we introduce WorldEcho, which evaluates action following over a broader action distribution through visual integrity and SE(3) end-effector trajectory alignment. Our diagnosis shows that expert-trained models perform better on demonstrated actions but struggle with off-expert trajectories, producing motion inconsistent with the commanded actions or visually invalid rollouts. To mitigate these failures, we propose WorldSync, which broadens action coverage, grounds intermediate video representations in action-induced robot dynamics through an Action-Forcing Expert, and aligns predicted and ground-truth changes under action interventions. Experiments show that WorldSync reduces integrity-gated error on RoboTwin and, when used for iterative policy improvement, yields higher success rates in simulation and on real robots.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Beyond Pattern Matching in 3D MLLMs: Part-Level Functional Reasoning for Generalizable Recognition
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Weihong Li, Hao Jiang, Yaohua Zha, Tao Dai, Shu-Tao Xia
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The paper introduces PFIR, a method enhancing 3D object recognition by employing part-level functional reasoning, significantly improving accuracy on geometrically ambiguous objects.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: 3D MLLMs recognize objects via pattern matching, which fails when geometrically similar objects require functional reasoning to disambiguate (e.g., dresser vs. wardrobe). Our per-sample Geometric Confusion Score (GCS) exposes this failure: baseline accuracy is 33.7% on ModelNet40's most ambiguous 20% versus 84.0% on its least ambiguous 20%. We identify a function-as-annotation pattern, in which functional language decorates a known identity instead of supporting inference, and hypothesize that reversing this information flow should concentrate improvements on the most ambiguous samples. PFIR (Part-level Functional Inference for Recognition) reverses that flow. Built on PartNeXt part segmentation, its data pipeline produces 507K QA pairs with functional CoTs (geometry $\to$ function $\to$ identity), and its progressive curriculum culminates in dual-objective GRPO: strict functional reasoning and descriptive grounding for Objaverse's diverse distribution. The two RL objectives yield nearly orthogonal task vectors ($\cos = 0.056$), enabling composition via Task Arithmetic. Under a strict dual OOD protocol (Objaverse $\to$ ModelNet40; XYZRGB $\to$ XYZ-only), PFIR raises zero-shot accuracy from 60.5% to 66.7%, with gains concentrated $2.6\times$ more on geometrically ambiguous samples---supporting part-level functional reasoning as an effective route to more generalizable 3D recognition. Code: https://github.com/this233/pfir-3d.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: This paper reviews and analyzes the integration of reinforcement learning into diffusion models, addressing limitations and proposing strategies for improved generation and real-world applicability.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: HGWM: Hierarchical Graph-Guided World Model for Zero-Shot Object Navigation via Graph Matching
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The HGWM model enhances zero-shot object navigation by integrating a room-anchor prior with spatial-semantic memory, achieving improved success rates and path efficiency in simulated environments.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Zero-shot object navigation requires an embodied agent to choose where to search while retaining evidence from previous observations. HGWM couples an LLM-generated room-anchor prior with persistent spatial-semantic memory. A coarse stage assigns visual-semantic scores to candidate headings on a 0-10 scale; a fine stage measures symbolic compatibility between observed objects, room context, and the goal prior. Phase-dependent fusion combines these scores with an LLM direction recommendation before local action selection. On HM3D v0.1, the reported HGWM configuration achieves 62.6% success rate (SR) and 31.5% success weighted by path length (SPL), compared with 58.1% and 31.2% for WMNav. On MP3D, the corresponding values are 46.8% and 17.9%, compared with 45.4% and 17.2%. The results indicate higher success point estimates and modest path-efficiency gains. On HM3D v0.2, the full model obtains 74.4% SR and 31.9% SPL. Additional component ablations reduce SR by 0.9-2.3 percentage points and SPL by 0.6-1.5 points. These are author-reported aggregate measurements. The accompanying implementation repairs pass offline tests; episode-level rerun records are not available. Evaluation is confined to simulation.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: MirrorCraft: Paired Evaluation under Hidden Rule Changes in Minecraft
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Jianxin Gao, Beini Hu, Runze Li, Hongjian Fang, Wanli Peng
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: MirrorCraft introduces a benchmark for evaluating LLM-based agents in Minecraft under hidden rule changes, revealing varied performance impacts across different rule suites.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: With the rapid progress of large language models (LLMs), an interesting question has emerged: how do LLM-based agents perform in Minecraft? To date, most Minecraft benchmarks evaluate them under fixed game mechanics, which are extensively documented online. High performance in these settings does not show whether an agent can continue making progress when familiar recipes, drops, and other rules change. In this paper, we introduce MirrorCraft, a paired benchmark for evaluating agents under hidden rule changes in Minecraft. Each Mirror world is a copy of its paired Vanilla world, with selected server-side rules silently modified by the datapack of one rule suite. Terrain, spawn, resource placement, task, interface, and action budget remain matched within every Vanilla-Mirror pair. MirrorCraft includes 10 Vanilla worlds in five controlled biomes, six rule suites, and three progression tasks, and we evaluate two LLMs and six agent configurations under a shared Mineflayer interface. We measure progress with server-verified advancement milestones and completion with success rate, and define the Rule Intervention Effect (RIE) as the performance change between paired Vanilla and Mirror worlds. Experiments with 8,640 episodes show that hidden rule changes have sharply different effects across suites. Among the configurations evaluated without rule descriptions, ReAct, Reflexion, and Voyager achieve the highest pooled Mirror Scores, but ReAct loses the most under compressed resource drops. Providing ReAct with the exact rules yields modest gains in average progress and completion across all three tasks, yet most of the difference between suites remains once the rules are known. MirrorCraft extends Minecraft evaluation beyond fixed mechanics and provides a controlled setting for studying how agents use gameplay outcomes when the rules of the current world differ from familiar ones.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Zongyao Zhao, Cheng-Jie Zhao, Ruihang Jiang, Bing Zheng, Zhaolin Wang
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The paper introduces Martingale GRPO (MART-GRPO), which optimizes failure feedback in VLA reinforcement learning by selectively truncating error contributions to enhance success rates.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: A failed vision-language-action (VLA) rollout does not imply that every action contributed to failure. Yet in group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), a single trajectory-level advantage is assigned to all actions in a rollout. Potentially useful recovery attempts can thus be penalized alongside the errors they aim to correct. Ideal stopping conditions for failure feedback are characterized using success-probability and policy-score martingales. At these stops, the removed gradient contribution has zero conditional expectation given the retained information. Truncation therefore preserves the expectation of a reference GRPO group-gradient estimator and can reduce its covariance. One such stop occurs when the conditional probability of success is zero, motivating error and recovery cues for selecting candidate feedback boundaries. Martingale GRPO (MART-GRPO) is introduced with a vision-language model (VLM) for event-guided truncation. The VLM is fine-tuned on our annotated training set using low-rank adaptation (LoRA). The last visible error without observed recovery is localized by the frozen VLM in complete rollout videos. Failure feedback is retained through the selected error interval and removed afterward, while successful-rollout loss terms and original loss normalization are preserved. For retrospective boundaries, changes in expectation and variance are analyzed to assess departures from ideal stopping. Experiments with OpenVLA-OFT on RoboTwin 2.0 show that MART-GRPO improves success rates over full-trajectory GRPO across multiple tasks.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: EgoForesight: Effectively Scaling Policy Learning with Noisy Egocentric Actions
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Chubin Zhang, Changyuan Wang, Yirui Wang, Ao Li, Shilin Ma
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: EgoForesight enhances policy learning by integrating noisy egocentric actions and robot demonstrations, improving performance and scaling through reliability-aware action learning and outcome-informed representation transfer.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Scaling policy learning requires broad experience and reliable supervision. Robot demonstrations provide high-quality trajectory supervision but are costly to collect. Egocentric videos broaden task and environment coverage, yet motion reconstruction and retargeting introduce noisy action labels. To address this challenge, we introduce EgoForesight, a vision-language-action framework that learns jointly from both sources by reducing the influence of unreliable action labels and exploiting demonstrated outcomes as complementary supervision. A joint vision-action flow couples future visual representation prediction with action generation, unifying reliability-aware action learning with outcome-informed representation transfer. Specifically, reliability-conditioned corruption allocates action supervision across noise levels according to source reliability, while reliability-weighted regression regulates each source's contribution. Complementing this treatment of noisy labels, privileged-future representation distillation draws supervision from demonstrated outcomes. An exponential-moving-average teacher observes the current scene and clean future to encode action-relevant structure from the resulting scene change. Its deeper representations supervise an earlier student layer receiving a corrupted future, providing outcome-informed structure beyond noisy action annotations. Together, these mechanisms support effective scaling with noisy egocentric actions. Over the tested range, EgoForesight exhibits steeper scaling slopes than the baseline, reducing real-world open-loop action MSE by 20.5% and improving RoboCasa few-shot success by 8.1 percentage points at 30,000 hours of pretraining data. After post-training, it also achieves strong absolute performance in both simulated and real-world dexterous manipulation.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: FORCA: A Force-Aware Coding Agent for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Xiao Tan, Yixuan Wang, Zhexi Wang, Wenzhen Yuan
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: FORCA is a coding agent that uses visual and force/torque inputs to autonomously generate Python programs for effective contact-rich robot manipulation without prior demonstrations or training.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Coding agents can translate language instructions into robot programs. For contact-rich manipulation, a key challenge is to generate and refine control logic that responds to physical interaction. We present FORCA, a coding agent that takes visual observations and wrist force/torque (F/T) measurements as input to write Python programs for contact probing and force-responsive motion. Between executions, the agent inspects force records alongside visual outcomes to diagnose failures and revise both motion and force-feedback control logic. FORCA requires no demonstrations, task-specific training, or simulation. Across five real-robot tasks, we demonstrate its effectiveness in three forms of contact-rich manipulation: improving manipulation accuracy, adapting to changes in object or surface properties, and regulating contact under surface variation and object motion. Compared with a vision-only variant of the same agent, FORCA improves grasp accuracy and task success and reduces contact loss in wiping and peeling.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: WorldMirror: Agentic Real-to-Sim Generation of Interactive Worlds from In-the-Wild Robot Demonstrations
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Tianling Xu, Weijie Wan, Honghao Su, Kailun Su, Junyuan Tang
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: WorldMirror is a framework that transforms real-world robot demonstrations into interactive digital twins through iterative refinement and high-fidelity scene reconstruction.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Existing approaches for robot learning in simulation often require substantial manual effort to construct scenes and specify tasks, limiting training scalability and data diversity. Meanwhile, in-the-wild robot demonstrations naturally provide diverse and realistic observations of real-world interactions. Leveraging these demonstrations for simulation requires both high-fidelity visual reconstruction and physically consistent interactions. General-purpose agents offer flexible adaptation to diverse scenarios and strong reasoning about 3D spatial relationships, while specialized generative models provide high-fidelity reconstruction of scene appearance and geometry. We introduce WorldMirror, an agentic real-to-sim framework that constructs interactive digital twins from in-the-wild robot demonstrations. Our central idea is to formulate real-to-sim construction as the iterative refinement of an executable world program. A coding agent decomposes the observed scene, plans reconstruction steps, and orchestrates specialized image and 3D generation tools, refining the program through verification feedback. A camera-pose-anchored scene representation organizes the world into static visual context, support geometry, and editable interactive assets while preserving spatial relationships among the scene, objects, and robot. The agent uses this representation to diagnose and correct reconstruction errors, enabling physically consistent interaction and trajectory replay. Experiments on DROID demonstrate that WorldMirror can reconstruct visually faithful and geometrically consistent interactive worlds while preserving the physical validity of recorded robot trajectories.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Robotic Spatiotemporal Editing: A Unified Interface for Controllable Action Generation via Masked Action Reconstruction
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Yanbang Li, Bu He, Yi Tian, Yu-Chiao Huang, Chenyu Zhang
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The paper presents the MAP interface for spatiotemporal control of robot actions, using an Inpainting Policy to unify and reconstruct action dimensions effectively.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Generative policies can synthesize robot behaviors, yet controlling and editing them through diverse spatiotemporal references remains challenging. In the real world, human intent requires robot behaviors that satisfy constraints on where, when, and how actions are executed. Our key insight is that spatiotemporal control references, such as keypoints, flows, orientations, and keyposes, can be viewed as partial specifications of the same temporal Cartesian action space. We introduce the MAP (Masked Action Space) interface to unify these action references and formulate controllable manipulation as an action inpainting problem. Our Inpainting Policy (IP) reconstructs missing action dimensions of the end-effector, combining progress-guided alignment with multi-mask training supporting unseen action-constraint combinations. We further adopt a training-free RePaint variant that iteratively inpaints the action during denoising to reduce control error. On ManiSkill and LIBERO-10, our policy achieves average task success rates of 92.67% and 64.67%, respectively.Real-world experiments demonstrate spatiotemporal control with average positional and rotational errors of 44.3 mm and 7°, respectively, showing that our policy can use diverse references to guide executable robot behaviors.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: WAM-TTT: Steering World-Action Models by Watching Human Play at Test Time
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Yusen Feng, Bingchen Han, Jiangran Lyu, Kai Liu, Yixin Zheng
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: WAM-TTT enables efficient adaptation of robot foundation models using unlabeled human videos at test time, enhancing performance without additional demonstrations or fine-tuning.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Steering robot foundation models (RFMs) toward new task variants or user-preferred behaviors remains challenging, often requiring additional robot demonstrations, task-specific fine-tuning, or long-context conditioning. We present WAM-TTT, a test-time training framework for steering world action models from raw human videos. Rather than treating human videos as trajectories to imitate, WAM-TTT absorbs them into a lightweight adaptive memory inside a frozen WAM through self-supervised video prediction. To make this memory useful for control, we introduce a meta-training stage that aligns human demonstrations with robot behaviors using paired human-robot data and a key--value memory reconstruction objective. At test time, only unlabeled human videos are required to adapt the memory, while the pretrained WAM remains frozen. This enables efficient and reusable steering without robot actions, human-side annotations, or task-specific fine-tuning, while preserving the generalization ability of the foundation model. Extensive experiments show that WAM-TTT consistently outperforms in-context human-video conditioning baselines across diverse manipulation tasks and generalization settings.

Jun MA老师实验室.title: Architecture-Aware Reinforcement Learning Makes Sliding-Window Attention Competitive in Math Reasoning
Jun MA老师实验室.authors_text: Kai Liu, Peijie Dong, Xinchen Xie, Jianfei Gao, Qipeng Guo
Jun MA老师实验室.summary: The paper presents SWARR, a method combining supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to enhance Sliding-Window Attention's performance in mathematical reasoning, addressing efficiency and accuracy gaps compared to self-attention.
Jun MA老师实验室.debug_abstract: The rapid progress of reasoning and agentic large language models (LLMs) has increased the demand for long-context inference, but self-attention (SA) scales quadratically with context length. To address this, we study SWARR (Sliding-Window Attention with Reinforced Adaptation for Math Reasoning), a practical recipe for adapting SWA models to mathematical reasoning. SWARR has two stages: (1) efficient conversion from a pretrained SA model to SWA with supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which avoids pretraining a new base model, and (2) policy adaptation with reinforcement learning (RL). We find that SWA still underperforms SA after SFT, and we hypothesize that this gap is caused in part by a data-architecture mismatch: most SFT data are prepared for SA models and may contain long-range dependencies that are difficult for SWA to model. Because on-policy RL optimizes self-generated trajectories under the SWA constraint, it can adapt trajectories to better match SWA. Experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks show that this recipe substantially narrows the gap between SWA and SA, recovering much of the accuracy lost during SWA conversion while preserving the efficiency benefits of linear-complexity attention. Our central contribution is the empirical finding that RL changes the conclusion one would draw from conversion and SFT alone about SWA's viability for math reasoning.

Jun MA老师实验室.title: From Visual Affinity to Learning Credit in Multimodal Reinforcement Learning

范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Kai Liu, Peijie Dong, Xinchen Xie, Jianfei Gao, Qipeng Guo

范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: The rapid progress of reasoning and agentic large language models (LLMs) has increased the demand for long-context inference, but self-attention (SA) scales quadratically with context length. 范明明老师实验室.title: From Visual Affinity to Learning Credit in Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Yuhang Han, Dingning Liu, Yujie Chen, Yaojie Zhang, Jingwei Song
范明明老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces Outcome-Conditioned Visual Credit (OVC), enhancing multimodal reinforcement learning by refining visual observation credit assignment to improve accuracy in predictive tasks.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves multimodal reasoning, but uniformly assigning a single response-level advantage to all tokens overlooks the distinct roles of visual observations and subsequent reasoning. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{Outcome-Conditioned Visual Credit (OVC)}, a plug-in framework that separates visual-association measurement from token-level credit assignment and is adaptable to policy-optimization methods with uniform response-level advantage allocation. Relative Visual Encoding constructs a context-relative visual coordinate by contrasting each predictive state's affinity to image and prompt-context representations. Outcome-conditioned Evidence Calibration combines this coordinate with uncertainty-scaled predictive features and calibrates their contributions to outcome-discriminative evidence through mean contrasts between positive- and negative-advantage responses, scaled by regularized within-side variation. Visual association thus informs credit through observed outcome differences rather than directly determining update priority. Normalized Credit Allocation conditions the calibrated evidence on the response's advantage sign to produce positive token weights with unit global mean. These detached weights preserve advantage signs while modulating individual token-gradient contributions. OVC reuses existing rollouts without auxiliary reward models, process annotations, or inference-time modules. Instantiated through GSPO-token, OVC retains sequence-level clipping and consistently improves six-benchmark mean accuracy over GSPO across three models, with gains of 1.86-2.39 percentage points.

范明明老师实验室.title: AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Yuanjian Xu, Jinyi Han, Jianing Hao, Yuxuan Sun, Fanyang Lu
范明明老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces AgentPerturb, a framework for evaluating LLM agent robustness against perturbations, revealing vulnerabilities and advocating for enhanced training methods to improve performance.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Real-world tasks are often complex and noisy, posing substantial challenges for LLM agents. Yet existing evaluations lack a systematic framework for jointly characterizing potential perturbation targets and types. Through controlled evaluations on APEX-Agents and Toolathlon, we find that perturbations consistently degrade performance, while the dominant vulnerabilities vary across task environments. A focused cost analysis further shows that successful perturbed trajectories can require substantially more computation. These findings motivate training objectives that cover diverse forms of noise and reward verification, uncertainty awareness, and recovery. We provide a rigorous benchmark-construction pipeline. Code and data will be released at https://github.com/xuyj233/AgentPerturb.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: ViT-H: Generative Video-To-Humanoid Control with Motion Tracking Feedback
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Zimo He, Tianyi Bian, Zizhong Yang, Hongjie Li, Nan Jiang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: ViT-H is a novel video-to-humanoid control framework that generates and optimizes humanoid motions directly from videos using motion-tracking feedback, outperforming traditional methods in quality and executability.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Learning humanoid control from monocular human videos offers a scalable way to acquire diverse whole-body behaviors. Yet, existing reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines are limited in system-level scalability by separately optimized intermediate stages and cannot directly optimize reference motion executability using downstream tracking feedback. We present ViT-H, a video-to-humanoid control framework following a generation-and-tracking paradigm. ViT-H directly generates humanoid reference motions from videos with a diffusion model, bypassing human motion reconstruction and retargeting, and uses motion-tracking outcomes to post-train the generator with direct preference optimization. We further introduce an autoregressive variant that enables real-time humanoid video teleoperation with sub-400 ms latency. Extensive experiments on the Unitree G1 demonstrate that ViT-H outperforms state-of-the-art reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines in both motion quality and executability. We further show that ViT-H scales favorably with model size and with both pre-training and post-training data scale, while motion-tracking feedback consistently improves executability across different motion trackers.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Sixiang Chen, Jiaming Liu, Jixian Wu, Yichen Guo, Tinghao Wang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper introduces WorldEcho and WorldSync to evaluate and improve action-conditioned world models, enhancing their reliability for robotic policy learning by aligning generated futures with actual actions.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Action-conditioned world models increasingly serve as learned simulators for robotic policy improvement, yet their reliability rests on an unverified assumption: generated futures faithfully reflect the consequences of arbitrary valid actions. Systematic evaluation against action-specific ground truth remains limited beyond expert demonstrations. To address this gap, we introduce WorldEcho, which evaluates action following over a broader action distribution through visual integrity and SE(3) end-effector trajectory alignment. Our diagnosis shows that expert-trained models perform better on demonstrated actions but struggle with off-expert trajectories, producing motion inconsistent with the commanded actions or visually invalid rollouts. To mitigate these failures, we propose WorldSync, which broadens action coverage, grounds intermediate video representations in action-induced robot dynamics through an Action-Forcing Expert, and aligns predicted and ground-truth changes under action interventions. Experiments show that WorldSync reduces integrity-gated error on RoboTwin and, when used for iterative policy improvement, yields higher success rates in simulation and on real robots.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: See What I Need, Dream What I Want: A Navigation Foundation Model on a Self-Constructed Representation Space
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Jiawei Chen, Yinxi Wang, Zihan Yang, Meijun Gao, Yaowei Liu
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: RepresentNav introduces a self-constructed visual representation space for navigation policies, achieving state-of-the-art performance by predicting future scene representations and reducing collisions in real-world scenarios.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: What visual representation should a navigation policy act on? Navigation policies built on vision foundation models largely leave representation design to the encoders' pretraining objectives. We present RepresentNav, a navigation foundation model built on a self-constructed representation space: a visual representation constructed by the policy's own objectives from vision foundation models. RepresentNav builds this space with Representation Residuals, a compact three-layer transformer that attends over features spanning the full depth of multiple complementary vision foundation models, so that the policy learns to see what it needs for navigation. In the same space it dreams what it wants: before every action a latent chain-of-thought predicts the representation of the scene a moment ahead. The dream is trained end-to-end with the policy as a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), with a next-representation prediction loss and a regularizer on its targets. RepresentNav sets a new state of the art on VLNVerse, VLN-CE R2R, EVT-Bench, and two point-goal benchmarks, and its gains carry over to a physical robot amid clutter and moving people. On VLNVerse fine-grained, RepresentNav achieves 83.80% success, outperforming the previous state of the art by 20.05 percentage points, and on EVT-Bench distracted tracking it reaches 85.5% with a single camera (+10.1). With the same encoders, the self-constructed space clearly outperforms concatenating their outputs and learns to weight their layers unevenly, and a dream in it cuts collisions by a quarter. A single dreamed latent decodes into the depth, semantics, and 3D occupancy of the scene a moment ahead, more accurately than pretrained encoders applied to the real future frame, although occupancy is never supervised, and the rollout tracks the robot's own motion over the next second: the dream emerges as a compact latent world model.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: JANUS: Foreseeing Latent Risk for Long-Horizon Agent Safety
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Yuan Xiong, Linji Hao, Shizhu He, Ken Deng, Yequan Wang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The JANUS framework enhances long-horizon agent safety by training a guard model, Vanguard, to predict and prevent operational risks through multi-agent simulations and joint task optimization.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Agent safety is moving from content moderation toward preventing operational failures before tool-using agents act. We propose Janus, a foresight-oriented framework for long-horizon agent safety that trains guards to anticipate delayed risks from partial trajectories. Janus synthesizes diverse agent trajectories via multi-agent simulation and learns a shared policy with two coupled tasks: an anticipation task that forecasts safety-relevant futures and an adjudication task that decides safety from both the observed prefix and anticipated future. The two tasks are jointly optimized with CoAA-RL, which rewards forecasts by their utility for downstream safety judgment. The resulting guard model, Vanguard, blocks unsafe actions before execution. Across four agent-safety benchmarks, Vanguard improves average protection by 15.9 percentage points over baseline guards while increasing benign task completion by 5.1 percentage points.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: HGWM: Hierarchical Graph-Guided World Model for Zero-Shot Object Navigation via Graph Matching
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The HGWM model enhances zero-shot object navigation by integrating a room-anchor prior with spatial-semantic memory, achieving improved success rates and path efficiency in simulated environments.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Zero-shot object navigation requires an embodied agent to choose where to search while retaining evidence from previous observations. HGWM couples an LLM-generated room-anchor prior with persistent spatial-semantic memory. A coarse stage assigns visual-semantic scores to candidate headings on a 0-10 scale; a fine stage measures symbolic compatibility between observed objects, room context, and the goal prior. Phase-dependent fusion combines these scores with an LLM direction recommendation before local action selection. On HM3D v0.1, the reported HGWM configuration achieves 62.6% success rate (SR) and 31.5% success weighted by path length (SPL), compared with 58.1% and 31.2% for WMNav. On MP3D, the corresponding values are 46.8% and 17.9%, compared with 45.4% and 17.2%. The results indicate higher success point estimates and modest path-efficiency gains. On HM3D v0.2, the full model obtains 74.4% SR and 31.9% SPL. Additional component ablations reduce SR by 0.9-2.3 percentage points and SPL by 0.6-1.5 points. These are author-reported aggregate measurements. The accompanying implementation repairs pass offline tests; episode-level rerun records are not available. Evaluation is confined to simulation.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: Semantic Anchoring for Robotic Action Representations
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Yuan Xu, Youheng Shi, Chengyang Li, Wentao Zhu, Yizhou Wang
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: The paper presents a method to anchor robotic action representations to a semantic manifold, improving task success and generalization in Vision-Language-Action models.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models inherit rich semantic representations from pretrained Vision-Language Models, yet fine-tuning on limited robot demonstrations degrades this structure and undermines generalization. A fundamental question therefore arises: what constitutes a good action representation? Inspired by the mirror neuron theory's insight that observation and execution share an intention-level encoding, we examine whether a robot's action representations preserve the semantic structure captured by pretrained encoders. Systematic probing confirms that this structure erodes during finetuning, and that its quality synchronizes with both task success and out-of-distribution generalization. We further introduce a plug-and-play method that anchors action representations to a semantic manifold while decomposing representations into a shared semantic channel and a private channel, all discarded at inference, leaving the deployed model unchanged. Validated on different VLA backbones across simulation and real-world benchmarks, our method yields up to +18.7% on real-world in-distribution tasks and +21.5% on out-of-distribution generalization.

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).title: EagleVLA: Towards Onboard Real-Time Robot Control via Foresight-Aligned Asynchronous Inference
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Zebin Yang, Qi Wang, Yunhe Wang, Xiurui Guo, Bo Yu
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).summary: EagleVLA enhances onboard Vision-Language-Action model efficiency through foresight-aligned asynchronous correction, achieving significant improvements in control frequency and success rates on low-power devices.
具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have achieved impressive performance on diverse embodied tasks. However, deploying VLA models on low-power onboard devices, such as the Jetson Orin, remains challenging due to their high computational complexity, which leads to substantial inference latency and low control frequency. 具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).authors_text: Tianling Xu, Weijie Wan, Honghao Su, Kailun Su, Junyuan Tang

具身感知与交互实验室 (EPIC Lab).debug_abstract: Existing approaches for robot learning in simulation often require substantial manual effort to construct scenes and specify tasks, limiting training scalability and data diversity. Meanwhile, in-the-wild robot demonstrations naturally provide diverse and realistic observations of real-world interactions. Leveraging these demonstrations for simulation requires both high-fidelity visual reconstruction and physically consistent interactions. General-purpose agents offer flexible adaptation to diverse scenarios and strong reasoning about 3D spatial relationships, while specialized generative models provide high-fidelity reconstruction of scene appearance and geometry. We introduce WorldMirror, an agentic real-to-sim framework that constructs interactive digital twins from in-the-wild robot demonstrations. Our central idea is to formulate real-to-sim construction as the iterative refinement of an executable world program. A coding agent decomposes the observed scene, plans reconstruction steps, and orchestrates specialized image and 3D generation tools, refining the program through verification feedback. A camera-pose-anchored scene representation organizes the world into static visual context, support geometry, and editable interactive assets while preserving spatial relationships among the scene, objects, and robot. The agent uses this representation to diagnose and correct reconstruction errors, enabling physically consistent interaction and trajectory replay. Experiments on DROID demonstrate that WorldMirror can reconstruct visually faithful and geometrically consistent interactive worlds while preserving the physical validity of recorded robot trajectories.

We present WAM-TTT, a test-time training framework for steering world action models from raw human videos. Rather than treating human videos as trajectories to imitate, WAM-TTT absorbs them into a lightweight adaptive memory inside a frozen WAM through self-supervised video prediction. To make this memory useful for control, we introduce a meta-training stage that aligns human demonstrations with robot behaviors using paired human-robot data and a key--value memory reconstruction objective. At test time, only unlabeled human videos are required to adapt the memory, while the pretrained WAM remains frozen. This enables efficient and reusable steering without robot actions, human-side annotations, or task-specific fine-tuning, while preserving the generalization ability of the foundation model. Extensive experiments show that WAM-TTT consistently outperforms in-context human-video conditioning baselines across diverse manipulation tasks and generalization settings.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: See What I Need, Dream What I Want: A Navigation Foundation Model on a Self-Constructed Representation Space
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiawei Chen, Yinxi Wang, Zihan Yang, Meijun Gao, Yaowei Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: RepresentNav introduces a self-constructed visual representation space for navigation policies, achieving state-of-the-art performance by predicting future scene representations and reducing collisions in real-world scenarios.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. 情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: HGWM: Hierarchical Graph-Guided World Model for Zero-Shot Object Navigation via Graph Matching
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The HGWM model enhances zero-shot object navigation by integrating a room-anchor prior with spatial-semantic memory, achieving improved success rates and path efficiency in simulated environments.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Zero-shot object navigation requires an embodied agent to choose where to search while retaining evidence from previous observations. HGWM couples an LLM-generated room-anchor prior with persistent spatial-semantic memory. A coarse stage assigns visual-semantic scores to candidate headings on a 0-10 scale; a fine stage measures symbolic compatibility between observed objects, room context, and the goal prior. Phase-dependent fusion combines these scores with an LLM direction recommendation before local action selection. On HM3D v0.1, the reported HGWM configuration achieves 62.6% success rate (SR) and 31.5% success weighted by path length (SPL), compared with 58.1% and 31.2% for WMNav. On HM3D v0.2, the full model obtains 74.4% SR and 31.9% SPL. Additional component ablations reduce SR by 0.9-2.3 percentage points and SPL by 0.6-1.5 points. These are author-reported aggregate measurements. The accompanying implementation repairs pass offline tests; episode-level rerun records are not available. Evaluation is confined to simulation.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents a method to anchor robotic action representations to a semantic manifold, improving task success and generalization in Vision-Language-Action models.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models inherit rich semantic representations from pretrained Vision-Language Models, yet fine-tuning on limited robot demonstrations degrades this structure and undermines generalization. HMI Lab.authors_text: Yuan Xu, Youheng Shi, Chengyang Li, Wentao Zhu, Yizhou Wang

HMI Lab.title: WorldMirror: Agentic Real-to-Sim Generation of Interactive Worlds from In-the-Wild Robot Demonstrations
HMI Lab.authors_text: Tianling Xu, Weijie Wan, Honghao Su, Kailun Su, Junyuan Tang

We introduce WorldMirror, an agentic real-to-sim framework that constructs interactive digital twins from in-the-wild robot demonstrations. Our central idea is to formulate real-to-sim construction as the iterative refinement of an executable world program. A coding agent decomposes the observed scene, plans reconstruction steps, and orchestrates specialized image and 3D generation tools, refining the program through verification feedback. A camera-pose-anchored scene representation organizes the world into static visual context, support geometry, and editable interactive assets while preserving spatial relationships among the scene, objects, and robot. The agent uses this representation to diagnose and correct reconstruction errors, enabling physically consistent interaction and trajectory replay. HMI Lab.title: WAM-TTT: Steering World-Action Models by Watching Human Play at Test Time
HMI Lab.authors_text: Yusen Feng, Bingchen Han, Jiangran Lyu, Kai Liu, Yixin Zheng
HMI Lab.summary: WAM-TTT enables efficient adaptation of robot foundation models using unlabeled human videos at test time, enhancing performance without additional demonstrations or fine-tuning.
HMI Lab.debug_abstract: Steering robot foundation models (RFMs) toward new task variants or user-preferred behaviors remains challenging, often requiring additional robot demonstrations, task-specific fine-tuning, or long-context conditioning. Rather than treating human videos as trajectories to imitate, WAM-TTT absorbs them into a lightweight adaptive memory inside a frozen WAM through self-supervised video prediction. To make this memory useful for control, we introduce a meta-training stage that aligns human demonstrations with robot behaviors using paired human-robot data and a key--value memory reconstruction objective. At test time, only unlabeled human videos are required to adapt the memory, while the pretrained WAM remains frozen. This enables efficient and reusable steering without robot actions, human-side annotations, or task-specific fine-tuning, while preserving the generalization ability of the foundation model. Extensive experiments show that WAM-TTT consistently outperforms in-context human-video conditioning baselines across diverse manipulation tasks and generalization settings.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: ViT-H: Generative Video-To-Humanoid Control with Motion Tracking Feedback
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Zimo He, Tianyi Bian, Zizhong Yang, Hongjie Li, Nan Jiang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: ViT-H is a novel video-to-humanoid control framework that generates and optimizes humanoid motions directly from videos using motion-tracking feedback, outperforming traditional methods in quality and executability.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Learning humanoid control from monocular human videos offers a scalable way to acquire diverse whole-body behaviors. Yet, existing reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines are limited in system-level scalability by separately optimized intermediate stages and cannot directly optimize reference motion executability using downstream tracking feedback. We present ViT-H, a video-to-humanoid control framework following a generation-and-tracking paradigm. ViT-H directly generates humanoid reference motions from videos with a diffusion model, bypassing human motion reconstruction and retargeting, and uses motion-tracking outcomes to post-train the generator with direct preference optimization. We further introduce an autoregressive variant that enables real-time humanoid video teleoperation with sub-400 ms latency. Extensive experiments on the Unitree G1 demonstrate that ViT-H outperforms state-of-the-art reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines in both motion quality and executability. We further show that ViT-H scales favorably with model size and with both pre-training and post-training data scale, while motion-tracking feedback consistently improves executability across different motion trackers.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Sixiang Chen, Jiaming Liu, Jixian Wu, Yichen Guo, Tinghao Wang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The paper introduces WorldEcho and WorldSync to evaluate and improve action-conditioned world models, enhancing their reliability for robotic policy learning by aligning generated futures with actual actions.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Action-conditioned world models increasingly serve as learned simulators for robotic policy improvement, yet their reliability rests on an unverified assumption: generated futures faithfully reflect the consequences of arbitrary valid actions. Systematic evaluation against action-specific ground truth remains limited beyond expert demonstrations. Our diagnosis shows that expert-trained models perform better on demonstrated actions but struggle with off-expert trajectories, producing motion inconsistent with the commanded actions or visually invalid rollouts. 智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: See What I Need, Dream What I Want: A Navigation Foundation Model on a Self-Constructed Representation Space
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Jiawei Chen, Yinxi Wang, Zihan Yang, Meijun Gao, Yaowei Liu
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: RepresentNav introduces a self-constructed visual representation space for navigation policies, achieving state-of-the-art performance by predicting future scene representations and reducing collisions in real-world scenarios.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: What visual representation should a navigation policy act on? Navigation policies built on vision foundation models largely leave representation design to the encoders' pretraining objectives. RepresentNav builds this space with Representation Residuals, a compact three-layer transformer that attends over features spanning the full depth of multiple complementary vision foundation models, so that the policy learns to see what it needs for navigation. The dream is trained end-to-end with the policy as a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), with a next-representation prediction loss and a regularizer on its targets. On VLNVerse fine-grained, RepresentNav achieves 83.80% success, outperforming the previous state of the art by 20.05 percentage points, and on EVT-Bench distracted tracking it reaches 85.5% with a single camera (+10.1). A single dreamed latent decodes into the depth, semantics, and 3D occupancy of the scene a moment ahead, more accurately than pretrained encoders applied to the real future frame, although occupancy is never supervised, and the rollout tracks the robot's own motion over the next second: the dream emerges as a compact latent world model.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: This paper reviews and analyzes the integration of reinforcement learning into diffusion models, addressing limitations and proposing strategies for improved generation and real-world applicability.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).title: JANUS: Foreseeing Latent Risk for Long-Horizon Agent Safety
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).authors_text: Yuan Xiong, Linji Hao, Shizhu He, Ken Deng, Yequan Wang
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The JANUS framework enhances long-horizon agent safety by training a guard model, Vanguard, to predict and prevent operational risks through multi-agent simulations and joint task optimization.
智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).debug_abstract: Agent safety is moving from content moderation toward preventing operational failures before tool-using agents act. 智元机器人联合实验室 (PKU-Agibot).summary: The HGWM model enhances zero-shot object navigation by integrating a room-anchor prior with spatial-semantic memory, achieving improved success rates and path efficiency in simulated environments.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: UAV-SwarmAgent: Scalable Multi-UAV Reconnaissance and Task Allocation via Code Generation and Vision-Language Reasoning
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Oleg Sautenkov, Yasheerah Yaqoot, Muhammad Ahsan Mustafa, Grigorii Kalinin, Chih-Yung Wen
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: UAV-SwarmAgent enables efficient multi-UAV reconnaissance through natural language commands, automated route generation, and vision-language reasoning, achieving high mission success rates in simulations.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Supervising a multi-UAV reconnaissance mission usually means plotting waypoints and watching every drone. We present UAV SwarmAgent, a hierarchical multi-agent system in which an operator states the mission in one natural-language sentence and a ground-station agent writes and executes code that turns it into per-UAV routes. The agent grounds inspection targets in an aerial map with a vision-language model, splits them among N UAVs by balancing route length, and dispatches worker agents that verify incidents with a compact onboard decision model. In simulation over 4 incident types and 3 foundation models, the swarm located the incident in 244 of 255 missions (95.7%). A paired scaling study with one to 5 UAVs shows that flight time follows an Amdahl-type law. The second UAV delivers half of the attainable saving and the speedup is bounded at 1.52x. We discuss what this predictability, and the false alarms we observed, imply for an operator who supervises the swarm, and outline the user study needed to test it.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Algorithm Modelization: Transforming Optimization Algorithms into Evolvable Intelligence
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Jian Yao, Zhiyao Zhang, Yichen Li, Xingyu Wu, Kay Chen Tan
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The paper introduces Algorithm Modelization, a paradigm that transforms iterative optimization algorithms into trainable models capable of evolving and generalizing through learned computational experiences.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Can algorithms be learned and evolved as models, rather than repeatedly redesigned as programs? We explore this question by introducing Algorithm Modelization, a new paradigm that turns iterative algorithms into trainable models. Its central idea is to regard algorithm execution trajectories as computational experience: by learning how algorithmic states evolve over iterations, a model can internalize the knowledge embodied in existing algorithms, reproduce their computational behaviors, and further evolve beyond them through training. As a first realization of this paradigm, we modelize iterative optimization as an autoregressive process, where preceding generations constitute the computational context for generating the next population. We develop a dimension-independent population-temporal architecture to capture both population interactions and iterative dynamics, together with an imitation-to-surpassing learning framework that first acquires algorithmic knowledge from heterogeneous teachers and then improves the resulting optimizer directly through optimization feedback. The modelized optimizer consequently goes beyond reproducing individual algorithms: it consolidates heterogeneous search knowledge into a single trainable model, achieves stronger optimization capability through subsequent improvement, and generalizes its acquired knowledge across problems and substantially larger unseen dimensions. More fundamentally, Algorithm Modelization makes algorithmic capability accumulable through learning, where new algorithms and problem-solving experience can become training resources for progressively improving the model. Our results establish a promising path from manually designed algorithms toward general algorithm models that learn, generalize, and evolve from computational experience.

机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).title: Train4Merge: RL or SFT---Which Yields Better Teachers for OPD-Based Model Merging?
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).authors_text: Jingyuan Huang, Zuming Huang, Yucheng Shi, Zhongzhi Li, Xiaoming Zhai
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).summary: The study compares reinforcement learning (RL) and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) as training methods for teachers in on-policy distillation, finding RL yields superior student performance in model merging.
机器人与机械智能实验室 (ROMI Lab).debug_abstract: Domain experts trained from a shared checkpoint can transfer their specialized capabilities to a single student through on-policy distillation (OPD). Existing research primarily focuses on improving this merging process, while the algorithms used to train the experts have received limited systematic comparison. We investigate which training algorithm produces teachers better suited to OPD through controlled single-teacher comparisons of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) across Agentic, Reasoning, and Perception. We further examine whether this advantage extends to multi-teacher OPD (MOPD). Teachers and students share the same Qwen3.5-9B initialization, and the two teacher types are compared at similar task performance. Our single-teacher experiments show that RL teachers yield stronger students and higher recovery of teacher performance gains across all three domains. In MOPD, the RL teacher group also yields a student with a higher three-domain mean score and higher overall teacher gain recovery than the SFT teacher group. Our further analysis shows that RL teachers undergo smaller parameter displacements from the shared initialization than SFT teachers. Teacher--student Top-K overlap also increases faster early in OPD or remains consistently higher with RL teachers than with SFT teachers. These findings support the hypothesis that RL teachers' smaller departures from the student's starting point facilitate learning through OPD, resulting in stronger students.
